rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a reader can't resolve what a pronoun/noun points to. Not present — 'the machine you just met' (chunk 0, line 3) and 'the fix'/'the failing test'/'the bug' (chunk 3 line 23, chunk 4 line 27) are module-lived-artifact references covered by the closer carve-out (this lecture sits directly after M1's Ex1-Ex3); 'the mirror'/'the chain' (chunk 5) are same-file callbacks to terms named in chunks 1 and 3 respectively. No forward references, no unresolved pronouns found.

Harm prevented: pointing at another file by position only, so resolution depends on deck-start config. Not present — the sole cross-file pointer, 'the opening lecture's mirror' (chunk 1, line 9), is unpacked in the same sentence ('the LLM that flatters you, calls unfinished work progress, mirrors your stance'), matching the rule's own worked pass-example verbatim. 'The multi-agent literature's term' (chunk 3) cites external literature, not a curriculum file position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a named beat (exercise/lecture) was cut or renamed, stranding the reference. Not present — body never names a specific exercise/lecture title to check for existence; the only backward-pointing nouns ('the fix', 'the failing test', 'the bug') are generic session-artifact references resolved against whatever the student's own M1 exercises produced, not a fixed beat that could go dead under a rechunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read (guess-before-reveal ordering)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a reveal narrated above its own guess-line, breaking a live-demo beat on a text read. Not present — this lecture contains no guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body; it is straight declarative teaching, not a live-demo beat.

Harm prevented: a chunk that says nothing standalone (a single wait-state bullet). Not present — chunks 1-5 each carry 3-4 substantive bullets with independent claim + mechanism content; chunk 0 carries a full thesis sentence plus the bring/build/ask frame.

Harm prevented: a header the chunk's own content contradicts. Not present — each header (preference round / scrollback is not the work / check resets the chain / answers in essays / machine is steerable) is a literal summary borne out by that chunk's bullets, including the new 'scrollback is not the work' slide, whose bullets (abstraction-by-necessity, architecture-diagram analog, disk-as-current-state) all support the header without softening or overreaching per the maintainer accept-note's guards.

Harm prevented per sub-item, none present: (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' — absent throughout. (b) Anaphora/epistrophe triples — chunk 5's bring/build/ask triad repeats 'steered by what you ___' across three bullets, but each leg (posture/external check/prompt request) carries distinct concrete mechanism and the triad is the lecture's own established thesis frame from chunk 0's lede, not a filler tic. (c) Self-grading superlatives (blocking sub-item) — none found anywhere in body. (d) Number + own retraction — the nine-in-ten/seven-step line (chunk 3, line 21) is explicitly maintainer-attested as deliberate (zombie-stat guard note in maintainer block), accept-with-note per rule's own exception clause. (e) Abstraction-noun stacks — none found; body stays concrete ('machinery under the mirror', 'a fresh read' etc., not stacked abstractions). (f) Verb triplets with an empty leg — 'flatters you, calls unfinished work progress, mirrors your stance' (chunk 1) has three distinct, concretely-answerable legs, no filler verb.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: repo/authorial vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections) projected on a wall where a student can't parse it. Not present — scanned all five chunks plus lede/kicker; no instances of the banned terms. Ordinary engineering words used throughout (chain, check, fix, shape, posture) are not repo-internal dialect.
